activated_parameters.description: The subset of a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model’s parameters that are actually used (activated) for processing a given input, typically through selected expert networks.

application.description: A way in which something can be used for a particular purpose. In the specific cases of LLMs, it refers to the practical uses or domains where the model is applied (e.g., chatbots, code generation).

attention_mechanism.description: The method a model uses to selectively focus on the most relevant parts of the input when generating or processing each token.

base_model.description: The original pre-trained model that serves as the foundation for subsequent fine-tuning, adaptation, or specialization.

benchmark_result.description: The model’s measured performance on a specific benchmark, including the evaluation metric and corresponding score.

blog_post.description: Any associated blog posts providing additional context, explanations, or updates about the model.

carbon_emitted.description: measured in "metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent." It is a unit of measurement used to express the amount of greenhouse gas emissions produced by human activities, such as burning fossil fuels, industrial processes, deforestation, agriculture, and recently training large-scale generative AI models. The term "equivalent" is used because different greenhouse gases have varying global warming potentials (GWP), meaning they trap different amounts of heat in the atmosphere over specific time frames.  Carbon dioxide (CO2) is the most common greenhouse gas emitted by human activities, but there are other greenhouse gases like methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O), which are more potent in terms of their heat-trapping ability compared to CO2. When calculating the total greenhouse gas emissions, the contributions of different gases are converted into a common unit of measurement, which is the metric ton of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2eq), to provide a standardized and comparable value for the total impact on climate change.  By using tCO2eq, it becomes easier to understand the overall environmental impact of various activities and implement strategies to reduce greenhouse gas emissions to mitigate climate change.

context_extension_method.description: The technique used during training or mid-training to extend a model’s supported context length, such as continued pre-training with longer sequences or positional-encoding methods like RoPE scaling.

context_length.description: It refers to the maximum number of tokens (words, characters, or subword units) the model can process in a single input sequence. It determines how much prior information the model can consider when generating or predicting the next tokens. A longer context length allows the model to understand and utilize more extensive contextual information, which is crucial for handling complex tasks, such as summarization, dialogue, or document-level analysis.

context_length_max.description: The maximum context length (in tokens) the model is trained or adapted to support, which can be increased during mid-training to enable processing longer sequences.

date_created.description: The date on which the CreativeWork was created or the item was added to a DataFeed.

finetuning_data.description: In the context of large language models (LLMs), fine-tuning data refers to a curated dataset used to further train a pre-trained model on specific tasks or domains. This data is typically domain-specific, task-oriented, or reflective of desired linguistic behaviors, allowing the model to adapt and perform more effectively in targeted applications. The quality, diversity, and relevance of the fine-tuning data are critical for achieving optimal model performance.

finetuning_task.description: The specific task or objective for which the pretrained model was fine-tuned.

fusion_architecture.description: The architectural design used to combine information from multiple modalities, components, or processing streams into a unified model representation.

hardware_description.description: Details about the hardware configuration, such as the number of devices, memory size, or compute power.

hardware_used.description: The specific hardware setup employed for training (e.g., GPUs, TPUs).

innovation.description: Key breakthroughs or unique contributions introduced by the model (e.g., novel architectures or training techniques or capabilities).

model_family.description: The broader category or lineage to which the model belongs (e.g., GPT, Llama).

model_name.description: Short name of the model introduced or used as a resource. (e.g., GPT-4, BERT).

moe_configuration.description: The configuration of a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model, including the number of experts, experts activated per token, routing strategy, and related architectural settings.

number_of_attention_heads.description: The number of parallel attention heads in the model, each independently learning to capture different relationships and patterns within the input.

optimizer.description: The optimization algorithm used to train the model (e.g., Adam, SGD).

optimizer_innovation.description: The novel optimization technique, algorithm, or modification introduced to improve the efficiency, stability, or performance of model training.

organization.description: The entity or group responsible for developing the model (e.g., OpenAI, Google, Meta).

parameters.description: The total number of trainable parameters in the model.

parameters_millions.description: The peak number of parameters the AI model supports, often referring to the largest variant in a model family.

post_training_infrastructure.description: The computational infrastructure, tools, and systems used to support post-training processes such as fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and model evaluation.

pretraining_architecture.description: The underlying neural network design used during pretraining (e.g., transformer-based, RNN, CNN).

pretraining_corpus.description: The dataset or collection of text used during the pretraining phase.

pretraining_task.description: The primary objective or task used for training the model initially (e.g., causal language modeling, masked language modeling).

quantization_precision.description: The numerical precision (e.g., FP16, INT8, INT4) used to represent model parameters or computations after quantization.

reasoning_mode.description: The reasoning strategy or approach used by the model to perform multi-step reasoning and arrive at an answer.

reward_mechanism.description: The method used to define, calculate, and provide rewards or feedback that guides the model toward desired behavior during reinforcement learning.

rl_algorithm.description: The reinforcement learning algorithm used to optimize the model’s behavior based on rewards or feedback, such as PPO, GRPO, or DPO.

safety_defect_rate.description: The rate or proportion of model outputs identified as unsafe, harmful, or otherwise violating defined safety criteria during evaluation.

safety_evaluation_protocol.description: The standardized procedure used to assess a model’s safety, including the benchmarks, test scenarios, criteria, and evaluation methods applied.

source_code.description: Whether and where the model’s implementation code is available (e.g., GitHub link, open-source repository).

supported_language.description: It refers to the specific natural languages the model is trained to understand and generate. This property indicates the range of linguistic diversity the model can handle, including its ability to perform tasks such as text generation, translation, or understanding in those languages. A broader set of supported languages enhances the model's utility for global applications and multicultural contexts.

synthetic_data_generation_method.description: The method or technique used to generate artificial training or evaluation data, such as model-generated, rule-based, or programmatically generated data.

tokenizer.description: The method or tool used to preprocess text into tokens (e.g., Byte Pair Encoding, WordPiece).

tool_calling_format.description: The format or protocol used by the model to structure and represent tool calls, including how tool names, arguments, and responses are encoded.

training_corpus_size.description: The scale of the pretraining dataset, measured in billions of tokens.

training_environment_scale.description: The scale of computational resources used to train the model, including the number and type of GPUs/accelerators, compute capacity, and distributed training setup.

training_pipeline.description: The sequence of training stages and procedures used to develop the model, such as pre-training, mid-training, continued pre-training, and post-training.

vision_encoder.description: The model component that processes visual inputs such as images and converts them into feature representations that can be understood by the language model.

weight_clipping_mechanism.description: The method used to constrain or clip model weight values within a specified range during training to improve numerical stability and prevent extreme weights.
